title: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
content:
A complete blood count (CBC) is a blood test. It's used to look at overall health and find a wide range of conditions, including anemia, infection, and leukemia.

A CBC measures several parts of your blood:

Red blood cells, which carry oxygen throughout your body. The red blood cell count (RBC) measures the number of red blood cells. Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. The hemoglobin test measures how much hemoglobin is in your blood. Hematocrit measures the percentage of your blood that is made up of red blood cells.

White blood cells, which fight infection. The white blood cell count (WBC) measures the number of white blood cells in your blood. High numbers of white blood cells may mean you have an infection or inflammation. Low numbers may mean you have certain health conditions.

Platelets, which help your blood clot and stop bleeding. The platelet count measures the number of platelets in your blood.

Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) is a measure of the average size of your red blood cells. Mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) is a measure of the average amount of hemoglobin in your red blood cells. Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) is a measure of the average concentration of hemoglobin in your red blood cells.

Normal ranges:
- Hemoglobin: 12.0-16.0 g/dL (women), 14.0-18.0 g/dL (men)
- Hematocrit: 36-46% (women), 41-53% (men)
- WBC: 4,500-11,000 cells/mcL
- Platelets: 150,000-400,000 cells/mcL
- RBC: 4.0-5.5 million cells/mcL
